item.title: Inside Sephoria’s return to Los Angeles this weekend
item.description: Sephoria, Sephora’s large-scale consumer event that launched in 2018, opened in Los Angeles on Friday for two days of ticketed, immersive activations from more than 65 brands for around 8,000 consumers. Glossy sat down with Sephora CMO Zena Arnold at the event on Friday to learn about the goals, challenges and future plans for the 8-year-old event.

item.title: Remedy Place launches a 'smart NAD injection pen' — and 'smart peptide pens' could be next
item.description: Glossy sat down with Remedy Place founder Dr. Jonathan Leary to learn about the bi-coastal wellness club’s first NAD "smart injection pen" launch. A partnership with U.K.-based NADclinic, the new pens allow users to order online and inject the popular coenzyme several times per week over the course of a month, replacing IV drips and supplements. Now, Dr. Leary is planning peptide and vitamin smart pens, like BPC-157 and vitamin D, as demand surges.

item.title: Ugg leans into craft and comedy for Fluff Yeah comeback campaign
item.description: When UGG brought back its Fluff Yeah sandal on March 16, the move was driven less by nostalgia and more by sustained consumer demand, according to the brand. The style, which first launched in fall 2018 at around $100, quickly became a celebrity favorite and a breakout product for the brand.

item.title: Beauty Briefing: What's behind the monobrand perfume store boom
item.description: This week, I looked into the spate of perfume stores opening in New York and across the globe. Additionally, Puig shakes up its C-suite with a new CEO and CFO, and both L’Oréal and Estée Lauder have their eye on the Indian beauty market.

item.title: Exclusive: Tarte founder Maureen Kelly enters nootropics with Finnsul, co-founded with her Gen-Z sons
item.description: Maureen Kelly famously launched Tarte from her one-bedroom apartment in 1999. Twenty-six years later, she's debuting a second brand, Finnsul, with her two sons, Finn and Sully McDonough. The founders have bootstrapped the brand from Kelly's renovated garage. Finn is 18 and will be heading to college soon; Sully is 19 and a freshman at the University of Miami.

item.title: The Glossy Podcast: As Middle East conflict escalates, luxury faces mounting pressure
item.description: On this week’s episode of the Glossy Podcast, senior fashion reporter Danny Parisi and international reporter Zofia Zwieglinska are joined by Achim Berg, founder of the fashion and luxury think tank FashionSights and former senior partner at McKinsey, to unpack how escalating conflict in the Middle East is impacting the global fashion and luxury industry.

item.title: Lancôme gets serious about longevity with new skin-care line
item.description: Longevity has quickly become one of beauty’s most crowded areas, fueled by demand for preventative health, supplements and clinic treatments. Now, Lancôme is making its play, and it’s doing so in a way that puts its claims under immediate scrutiny.

item.title: Luxury Briefing: In a volatile Middle East, bags charms reaching $250,000 are catching on
item.description: For this week's Luxury Briefing, I spoke with designer and founder of Bag Bijoux Ashna Mehta about why high jewelry is moving onto handbags.

item.title: What's driving the beauty bag charm trend
item.description: It was nearly 10 years ago, in 2017, that Glossier first released a sweatshirt. It was simple, with the name of the brand emblazoned across the front. And then, in 2024, Hailey Bieber reinvented the beauty merch wheel with the invention of the Rhode Lip Case. Now, charms are a booming beauty trend.

item.title: An exception to luxury’s slowed growth, Perigold eyes vacant department store locations amid expansion
item.description: Launched by Wayfair to be its luxury counterpart, 9-year-old Perigold is in growth mode — against all odds. In 2025, the home furnishings retailer opened its first two stores, in Houston and West Palm Beach. And just last month, it invested in its first major collaboration.

item.title: Dupe fragrance has hit the mainstream. Now what?
item.description: When dupe perfumes first hit the market, they existed largely on the periphery of the fragrance industry. Since then, dupe fragrance brands have exploded into the mainstream, entering major retailers, partnering with celebrities and occupying prime real estate. But within the fragrance industry, the term still elicits a certain hesitation — and in some cases, outright legal challenges.

item.title: Why TikTok Shop’s real ROI was never meant to stay on TikTok
item.description: Learn how TikTok Shop drives cross-channel growth, including Amazon search lift, retail demand and creator influence that boosts overall marketing ROI.

item.title: WNBA player Lexie Hull launches Forta, aimed at creating a new category of performance-driven makeup
item.description: In food and beverage, brands like Clif Bar and Gatorade were built to cater to athletes' needs and then became mainstream; the same is true for Lululemon and Athleta. But in beauty, no one has approached products this way. This is the thesis for a new brand called Forta, a play on "for the active."

item.title: Stitch Fix is targeting people mid-transition, from GLP-1 users to newly divorced men
item.description: Stitch Fix is targeting customers in moments of change, including using a GLP-1 or divorcing, as new data and earnings show rising engagement and spending.

item.title: How fragrance is winning on TikTok Shop
item.description: This week, I checked in on Snif’s explosive sales day on TikTok Shop thanks to Mikayla Nogueira, and what it means for the category and the retailer as a whole.
